crosswalk.crs_as_published: EPSG:4269/WGS84 reach points as NWM publishes them (v3.0 retrospective latitude/longitude); positions recorded as km along the banked HR centreline

newer_banked_not_published.why: a newer derived object of this layer is banked but has no geo_display_objects row; the published one above is served until it is published

crosswalk.served: the newest derived object with a publish row

source.terms_ref: docs/handback_2026_10_14_rivers_in_motion_recon.md Q1 (NOAA NODD terms quoted from the AWS Open Data registry: open; attribution requested; no implied endorsement)

newest_record_rule: the ingesters' own: the newest row per (kind, source_code, source_key) by fetched_at, then record_id, read through one LATERAL per key (geo_records holds two copies of every CWMS project; 57-66 are superseded by 67-76 and never served)

not_served.placed: a station's km, feature_id and dist_m are in the crosswalk object's places[<source_key>], which is on the display bucket; this route reads no R2 (d091763 §5). The object is keyed by record_sha256, so the page joins it against each record's own sha and applies: placed iff the place exists, its record_sha256 equals the record's, and dist_m <= 1000.

anchor.scale_why: attrs._bank.anchor.km_from_reach_start is an interval [lo, hi] on NHD's lengthkm scale, not the walk geometry's measure (D-09-25-237 §2): on the Columbia the two differ by about 4.5 km (Bonneville [727.887, 728.371] against the walk's 723.746). So it is served as the anchor it is, and the page snaps by geometry.
